rationale: The pi benchmark is a small, single-source, floating-point-heavy program dominated by one hot numeric loop, so the weight table favors low-overhead arithmetic and structural transforms over control-flow inflation: SUB and SPLIT get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with minimal cost weights because instruction substitution and basic-block splitting add real reversal friction at negligible runtime/size cost and preserve FP semantics reliably; FLA retains strong security/diversity weights since flattening a small function body is a potent defense, but its RuntimeCost weight is kept high (0.7) so the selector only applies it where the loop structure tolerates dispatch overhead, and its CorrectnessRisk weight (0.6) reflects FP-loop sensitivity to restructuring; BCF is deliberately down-weighted on SecurityGain (0.5) and up-weighted on RuntimeCost/SizeCost (0.7) because bogus predicates inside a hot FP loop multiply iterations for little analyst confusion in a tiny program; IBR is a moderate middle ground applied sparingly; ICALL is down-weighted since this program is call-sparse, so indirection buys little; and IGV is kept minimal (near-disable) because the profile shows essentially no global-variable surface to protect.
